person.name: Dong Hwi Kim
person.affiliation: Mechanical Engineering & Electrical and Computer Engineering · Seoul National University
person.intro: I am an undergraduate at Seoul National University studying Mechanical Engineering and Electrical and Computer Engineering. My interests span 3D vision and perception, control, robotics, and autonomous driving.
person.bio: At the RPM Robotics Lab, I work with Prof. Ayoung Kim on 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM and 3D mapping. At the AIDAS Lab, my collaboration with Prof. Jaeyoung Do focuses on visual data augmentation for robot learning using reconstructed scenes and robot kinematics.

research.title: Multi-View Demonstration Augmentation

research.summary: Multi-view robot demonstrations rendered from reconstructed Gaussian assets, calibrated cameras, and robot kinematics.

sections.heading: Metric alignment
sections.body: Check reconstruction scale against ChArUco calibration and robot CAD.

points.text: Compare distances between rigid robot parts against the URDF.
Hold scale fixed. Refine pose with iterative closest point (ICP) on high-opacity Gaussian cores.
Check robot and scene dimensions in the same coordinate system.

figure.alt: Repository figure comparing robot length-ruler errors and Gaussian-core distances before and after scale correction
figure.caption: Rigid-part distances check metric scale. Measurements refer to the repository’s reference capture.

sections.heading: Robot-link assets
sections.body: Assign each Gaussian to its nearest CAD link. Convert the captured robot into reusable link assets.

points.text: Apply inverse forward kinematics at the capture pose.
Reapply the capture pose. Compare the reconstructed and original posed geometry.

sections.heading: Kinematic replay and rendering
sections.body: Repose the link assets along a demonstration trajectory. Render all cameras from the same episode state.

points.text: Forward kinematics drives each articulated link.
Explicit attachment and release rules control grasped objects.
Update the wrist-camera pose with the robot. Keep standing cameras calibrated.

figure.alt: Four rendered stages of the same FR3 cube-stacking episode
figure.caption: Approach, grasp, and stacking in a rendered episode. The montage illustrates kinematic replay.

sections.heading: Capture-specific repairs
sections.body: Repair incomplete geometry before generating demonstrations.

points.text: Reconstruct a rolled capture separately. Merge only the surfaces missing from the static capture.
Replace reconstruction haze with a surface on the calibrated plane. Bound it by the measured table footprint.

sections.heading: Episode validation
sections.body: Apply acceptance checks before exporting an episode.

points.text: Check scale, FK round trips, grasp spacing, and object-pose continuity.
Check black frames and carried-object visibility in the wrist view.
Generation checks validate the rendered episode. Downstream robot-policy performance needs separate evaluation.

projects.title: Autonomous Object-Collecting Robot
projects.image_alt: Team 7's autonomous mecanum-wheel robot in the competition arena
projects.summary: An autonomous collection robot combining dual-camera segmentation, geometric target selection, and LiDAR/IMU-informed motion.
projects.role: Contributed across perception and model training, planning, data collection, hardware, and system integration with Team 7.

sections.heading: Robot platform and interfaces
sections.body: A Jetson Orin Nano runs perception and navigation. An ESP32 controls the four mecanum-wheel motors.

points.text: Body-velocity commands travel over USB serial. The controller converts them into wheel motion.
Wheel direction and feed-forward gains are calibrated. Motion commands include a duration and auto-stop.

sections.heading: Dual-camera perception
sections.body: YOLO segmentation processes both angled cameras. Their detections are merged into one UDP message.

points.text: Camera intrinsics and toe angles map detections into a common forward-facing view.
Confidence, range-normalized mask area, bearing, and arena-cell ownership filter candidate objects.

sections.formula: normalized area = mask area × (range / reference range)²

sections.heading: Collection and route planning
sections.body: The robot follows a fixed sweep route. Live detections determine when it collects an object.

points.text: The passive basket holds three objects. Forward motion captures; reverse motion can release the load.
A full basket interrupts the sweep. The robot returns to deposit its objects.
Alignment and return maneuvers must account for the loaded basket.

figure.alt: Official team repository diagram showing the object grid, storage corner, and robot start corner
figure.caption: Arena layout. The route links target collection to the delivery zone.

sections.heading: Localization and motion control
sections.body: LiDAR wall fitting estimates pose. Integrated IMU yaw terminates calibrated turn pulses.

points.text: LiDAR feedback corrects strafe motion. The timed alternative was disabled after calibration errors.
Stops use calibrated reverse-braking pulses. Cruise speed stays within the measured braking range.

sections.heading: On-device checks
sections.body: Inference speed and robot speed determine the observation window for each target.

points.text: Benchmark candidate models on the Jetson. Set detection gates for the available inference frames.
Check for frozen streams. Compare raw camera frames with motion logs during tuning.

projects.title: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
projects.image_alt: Team MRI reconstruction framework using brain and knee experts with Feature VarNet and FI VarNet
projects.summary: MRI reconstruction from undersampled k-space using Feature/FI VarNet, acquisition-specific experts, and model averaging.

sections.heading: Measurement-consistent reconstruction
sections.body: Feature VarNet and FI VarNet alternate learned updates with data-consistency operations.

points.text: Estimate sensitivity maps from multi-coil measurements.
Feature VarNet refines feature representations. FI VarNet also includes image-domain cascades.
Use the MRI encoding model to keep updates connected to acquired k-space samples.

sections.heading: Condition-specific experts
sections.body: Train separate experts for anatomy and acceleration. Use explicit rules to select them at inference.

points.text: Identify brain or knee inputs from coil count under the challenge data conventions.
Read the sampling mask to select a 4× or 8× model.

sections.heading: Training pipeline
sections.body: MRI-aware augmentation increases training diversity. AdamW and warmup/cosine scheduling support optimization.

points.text: Use small rotations, shearing, and horizontal flips. Increase augmentation strength during training.
Use DeepSpeed and activation checkpointing for the reconstruction models.
Resume interrupted runs. Convert distributed checkpoint state into inference weights.

sections.heading: Averaging and ensembling
sections.body: The submission uses both weight averaging and output ensembling.

points.text: Average compatible model weights into one checkpoint. This adds no extra model forward pass.
Run configured Feature VarNet and FI VarNet pairs. Average their reconstructed images.

projects.overview: Recover brain and knee MRI images from undersampled multi-coil k-space. K-space contains the frequency-domain measurements. The challenge uses 4× and 8× acceleration.

projects.title: Chronological Ordering of Shuffled Images
projects.image_alt: Diagram of mapping frame-order views into a common coordinate system for Random4 inference
projects.summary: Chronological ordering of four shuffled frames using a LoRA-adapted vision-language model and constrained permutation decoding.

sections.heading: Vision-language adaptation
sections.body: Adapt Qwen3.5-27B with LoRA. Replace free-form answers with structured readouts.

points.text: Six readouts compare the temporal order of frame pairs.
Four readouts score the chronological positions.
Temporal-gap supervision and hard-negative ranking support the final training stage.

sections.heading: Constrained permutation decoding
sections.body: Combine pair and slot evidence. Score all 24 valid chronological orders.

points.text: Select the highest-scoring permutation. Each frame appears exactly once.
Convert the ordered sequence into per-input ranks. These are inverse permutations.

sections.heading: Random4 inference
sections.body: Evaluate four input-image orderings. Align their outputs before aggregation.

points.text: Map each view’s logits back to the original image identities.
Average the aligned logits. Apply the decoder to the combined evidence.
Test permutation mappings and the final submission format.

sections.heading: Snapshot averaging
sections.body: Average nine language-LoRA snapshots from one training trajectory. Accumulate parameters in CPU float32.

points.text: The result is one adapter. Parameter averaging adds no forward passes.
Random4 still requires four input-order evaluations.

projects.overview: Input: a sentence and four shuffled frames. Output: the chronological rank of each input frame.
result_notes: The score belongs to the official final-selected submission. Later Crop-TTA experiments are documented separately.

projects.title: Physics-Guided Wind Power Prediction
projects.image_alt: Zephyr Analytics team cover for the 2025 Wind Power Prediction Competition
projects.summary: Hourly wind-power forecasting with a physical power curve, LightGBM residual correction, and an optimized ensemble.
projects.role: Model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization.

sections.heading: Physical baseline
sections.body: Start with a turbine power curve. Estimate expected generation from the weather conditions.

points.text: Include air-density estimates. The team used the Arden–Buck equation in feature construction.
Use the physical relationship as the starting forecast.

sections.heading: Residual learning
sections.body: Compute the error between observed generation and the physical baseline. Train LightGBM to predict that residual.

points.text: Add the predicted residual to the baseline.
The learned component corrects the physical forecast’s remaining error.

sections.formula: hybrid forecast = physical baseline + learned residual

sections.heading: Ensemble optimization
sections.body: Combine the hybrid forecast with Ridge Regression and Random Forest predictions.

points.text: Use Optuna to tune model hyperparameters and ensemble weights.
Report NMAE and the competition’s settlement revenue rate. Inspect site-wise distributions alongside the aggregate scores.

projects.credit: Cover, architecture, and evaluation images are from the original Zephyr Analytics team presentation, supplied by Dong Hwi Kim.

projects.title: Face-Tracking Pan–Tilt Camera
projects.image_alt: Sunflower-inspired face-tracking camera device with a yellow phone mount and white circular base
projects.summary: A Raspberry Pi pan–tilt camera that follows a face with proportional visual feedback and infrared manual control.

sections.heading: Hardware
sections.body: A Raspberry Pi connects the camera, servos, and infrared receiver.

points.text: Two servos rotate the camera horizontally and vertically.
A ball-transfer unit distributes load and reduces friction.

figure.alt: Exploded hardware diagram of the pan–tilt filming device
figure.caption: Camera mount, two servo axes, and ball-transfer support.

sections.heading: Face tracking and visual control
sections.body: Picamera2 supplies frames. OpenCV’s Haar-cascade detector finds faces; the largest detection becomes the target.

points.text: Normalize the face center’s offset from the image center.
Convert image error into incremental pan and tilt commands.
The final code sets derivative gains to zero. Visual feedback is proportional.
Clamp the commanded angles. Map them to calibrated pigpio pulse widths.

sections.heading: Remote control and device state
sections.body: A separate thread reads LIRC commands while tracking runs.

points.text: Switch between automatic tracking and manual operation.
Move either axis, stop motion, or exit.
An LED indicates face detection. Shutdown stops the camera and disables servo pulses.

projects.title: Period-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
projects.image_alt: Original presentation slide showing the TaXer periodic feature extraction and cross-attention architecture
projects.summary: Time-series forecasting through transformer cross-attention to FFT-based periodic features or dilated causal convolutional features.

sections.heading: TaXer: periodic features
sections.body: Use TimesNet-style FFT analysis to select dominant periods.

points.text: Reshape each sequence according to the selected periods.
Apply 2D convolution to model variation within and across periods.

sections.heading: Transformer integration
sections.body: Project extracted features into the transformer embedding dimension.

points.text: Use variable-wise patch embeddings and a global token.
Broadcast projected temporal features across variables.
Let the sequence representation query the feature context.
Apply the forecast head. Restore each variable’s original scale.

sections.formula: temporal features → linear projection → cross-attention context

sections.heading: WaXer: convolutional alternative
sections.body: Replace periodic extraction with WaveNet-style dilated causal convolutions.

points.text: Keep the projection and transformer integration pattern.
Evaluate the alternative temporal prior. Compare forecast errors and model sizes.

projects.hero_caption: Hybrid forecasting architecture from the team presentation.
projects.result_summary: Course-project Sticker Sales MSE: TaXer 0.1569, TimeXer 0.1647; additional weather and model-size comparisons in the report.
projects.contribution_summary: Team project with Jinwoo Seo, Hyeonseop Shin, and Manyoung Han.
projects.overview: Test temporal feature extractors inside a transformer forecaster. Compare periodic and convolutional representations on weather and sales data.
result_notes: Course-project results under the reported setup. The report also covers weather data and model-size comparisons.
